title: Microsoft 365 Backup: 30-day backup and recovery for Microsoft Entra ID objects

reasons: published before the check existed: kept live with a notice while a corrected version is prepared

summary: Hold: the briefing assigns an enablement default, billing model and restore role to the planned 30-day extension without feature-specific documentation. Its Entra automation entry is a namespace description rather than an executable API call, and the billing instructions omit the different route for existing customers.

claims.claim: The planned 30-day extension is admin-opt-in.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Entra Backup Recovery 30 days Microsoft 365 Backup enable opt in roles. Read Entra overview and Backup setup; automatic seven-day backups and other workloads' setup do not state the extension's default.
claims.fix: Set defaultState to 'unknown'. State that the 30-day extension's default and enablement requirements are not stated; distinguish this from existing automatic seven-day Entra backups.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model; licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The planned Entra extension has a mixed licensing model combining included P1/P2 recovery with chargeable pay-as-you-go 30-day recovery.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Entra 30 day Backup Recovery pricing meter rate; "Entra" "30-day" "Backup" "pricing". Read Entra overview and Backup pricing, overview and setup. None explicitly assigns a charge or licensing model to the Entra extension.
claims.fix: Set licensing.model to 'unknown' for the extension. Say: 'The existing seven-day recovery is included with Entra ID P1/P2. Licensing and billing for the planned 30-day extension are Not yet published.' Describe existing Backup pay-as-you-go pricing only as separate context, not an established Entra charge.

claims.claim: The variable cost rating is established for this extension despite its unpublished licensing and meter.
claims.quote: cost: "variable"; "The Entra meter and rate are not yet published". The scale says: "If licensing is not yet published, rate the cost that is known (`low` when the only cost the sources show is admin time)".
claims.fix: Set cost to 'low' and the rationale to 'Low. Restore planning and testing require admin time; licensing, meter and rate for the 30-day extension are not yet published.' Do not use another workload's consumption model as an established charge for this change.

claims.claim: The Entra admin center has Backup and recovery with Overview, Backups, Difference Reports, Recovery History and Hard deletion protection pages.
claims.quote: select Backup and recovery in the left navigation pane. These pages are available: ... Overview ... Backups ... Difference Reports ... Recovery History ... Hard deletion protection (preview)
claims.fix: Retain the navigation labels: the pre-check's missing-word finding is not confirmed. Add '(preview)' to Hard deletion protection in the structured path and rendered table, as the cited page does.

claims.claim: 'entraRecoveryServices resources (Microsoft Graph beta)' supplies the automation call for Entra backup, difference reports and recovery.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Graph entraRecoveryServices list snapshots beta v1.0 directory recovery snapshots. Read the cited Entra API overview and List snapshots excerpts. entraRecoveryServices is a namespace, not an HTTP method and endpoint.
claims.fix: Replace the namespace description with a real, versioned documented operation and scope the row accordingly. For listing backups, use 'GET /v1.0/directory/recovery/snapshots' and cite https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/api/entrarecoveryservices-recovery-list-snapshots?view=graph-rest-1.0. Do not imply this GET performs recovery; describe preview and recovery operations separately using their references.

claims.claim: The Entra and Microsoft 365 admin center recovery experiences will eventually converge.

claims.fix: Replace 'until the experiences converge' with 'under the experience split described by the roadmap'. Keep any possible convergence explicitly an open question, not a promised product direction.

claims.claim: The cited tenant backup overview labels the Entra recovery Graph surface as beta.
